gap: No result ChatGPT got says that BLUETTI's and EcoFlow's boost modes do not raise rated output. BLUETTI says Power Lifting is for pure-resistive heating devices like hair dryers, kettles and heaters. EcoFlow says X-Boost works by lowering voltage, so results vary by device. That means an 1,800 W induction plate has to fit under the station's rated continuous output, and a station like the BLUETTI AC180 (1,800 W rated, 2,700 W Power Lifting) gives it no headroom.
standout_why: I checked the cited BLUETTI AC200L page (bluettipower.com/pages/ac200l). It gives 'Power lifting Mode: 3,600W' but never says which devices that mode suits, and it never mentions induction. Its FAQ only says to keep the total under the rated 2,400 W. I also checked the uncited result ankersolix.com/f2000. It lists Inverter Mode 2,400 W and Bypass Mode 1,440 W but says nothing about cooktops or SurgePad device limits. ChatGPT's answer says to get 2,000 W or more continuous but never says why boost or surge figures don't count. I could not open the other cited page, unpluggedwatts.com, because of a certificate error, so I have not confirmed that it lacks this point.
decides: It backs the page's 'At its limit' rows (AC180, P1800, DELTA 3 Plus, all 1,800 W). The maker's boost mode does not give headroom for an induction plate, so for an 1,800 W plate like the Duxtop 9100MC the pick should be a station rated 2,000 W or more continuous: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 or EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max. Separately, the F2000's 1,440 W Bypass Mode limit suggests a full-power 1,800 W plate would be over that limit while the unit runs on wall power. That reading is my inference from Anker's spec; Anker does not say it about cooktops.
